Descrivi il nodulo in B-mode e il suo co: Describe the nodule on B-mode and its behavior after contrast, taking the timing into account. What category would you assign and what do you do?
In CEUS il tempo conta: la fase arterios: In CEUS, timing matters: the arterial phase runs from about 10-20 to 30-45 seconds, then the portal phase up to 2 minutes and the late phase until the microbubbles disappear (4-6 minutes). Hepatocellular carcinoma typically enhances in the arterial phase (non-rim hyperenhancement) and then shows late (after 60 seconds) and mild washout; cholangiocarcinoma and metastases often have early and marked washout (LR-M). This nodule, instead, remains isoenhancing in all phases on the available images and the arterial phase is documented by a single image at 19 seconds: with CEUS LI-RADS v2017 a nodule ≥ 10 mm without arterial hyperenhancement and without washout is LR-3 (intermediate probability). The final diagnosis in the collection is hepatocellular carcinoma: a proportion of hepatocellular carcinomas, especially well-differentiated ones, do not show the typical behavior on CEUS. The lesson is twofold: describe what you see, not what you expect from the diagnosis; and an indeterminate nodule in an at-risk patient must be followed up with multiphase contrast-enhanced CT or MRI (and possibly biopsy), not filed away. CEUS LI-RADS applies only to patients at risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B, prior hepatocellular carcinoma): here the clinical history is not provided by the collection.
CEUS: descrivi ciò che vedi in ogni fase: CEUS: describe what you see in each phase, with the time. Without arterial hyperenhancement and without washout, a nodule ≥ 1 cm is indeterminate (LR-3): it does not exclude hepatocellular carcinoma, it must be followed up with CT or MRI.
Diagnosi finale della collezione B-mode-: Final diagnosis of the B-mode-and-CEUS-Liver collection: hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). On the available CEUS images the nodule is isoenhancing (inconclusive CEUS).
